text_note.zh: 通行本和古籍原文有几处不同：通行本作“丧乱”“夫婿”“美如玉”“盈掬”，原文作“丧败”“夫壻”“已如玉”“盈匊”。“壻”是“婿”的异体字，“匊”同“掬”，意思一样。
text_note.en: The commonly taught text differs from the source text in a few places. It has sāng luàn (death and turmoil) for sāng bài (defeat and ruin), měi rú yù (lovely as jade) for yǐ rú yù (already like jade), and modern forms for the characters in fū xù (husband) and yíng jū (a full handful), which mean the same.

readings.zh: “丧乱”是死亡和动乱，“丧”读 sāng。
readings.en: Sāng luàn means death and turmoil; here the character is read sāng.

readings.zh: “恶”是“厌恶、讨厌”的意思，读 wù，不读 è。
readings.en: Here it means to dislike, so it is read wù, not è.

readings.zh: “那”在这里同“哪”，是“哪里、怎么”的意思，一般读 nǎ。
readings.en: Here it is the same as the word for "how", and is usually read nǎ.
Here it means hair, read fà.

readings.zh: 单用时口语读 báo，诗文朗读多读 bó。这里取 bó。
readings.en: On its own, meaning thin, it is read báo in speech; in poetry it is often read bó, as here.

glosses.zh: 绝代：当代独一无二的，世上少有的。
glosses.en: jué dài: one of a kind in her time, rare in the world.

glosses.zh: 佳人：美丽的女子。
glosses.en: jiā rén: a beautiful woman.

glosses.zh: 幽居：住在偏僻安静的地方。
glosses.en: yōu jū: to live in a quiet, out-of-the-way place.

glosses.zh: 空谷：没有人的山谷。
glosses.en: kōng gǔ: an empty valley where no one lives.

glosses.zh: 自云：自己说。
glosses.en: zì yún: she says herself.

glosses.zh: 良家子：好人家的女儿，出身清白的官宦人家。
glosses.en: liáng jiā zǐ: a daughter of a good family, here an official's family.

glosses.zh: 零落：像花叶凋落一样，指家道败落、流落无依。
glosses.en: líng luò: fallen like dead leaves, meaning her family has fallen and she has no one to rely on.

glosses.zh: 依草木：靠着草木生活，住在山林里。
glosses.en: yī cǎo mù: living among the grass and trees, in the wild hills.

glosses.zh: 关中：今天陕西中部一带，唐朝都城长安就在这里。
glosses.en: guān zhōng: the land within the passes, central Shaanxi today, where the Tang capital Chang'an stood.

glosses.zh: 昔丧乱：从前的战乱，指安史之乱时叛军攻进长安。
glosses.en: xī sāng luàn: the turmoil of the past, that is, when rebels took Chang'an during the An Lushan Rebellion.

glosses.zh: 杀戮：杀害。
glosses.en: shā lù: to be killed.

glosses.zh: 何足论：哪里值得一提，有什么用。
glosses.en: hé zú lùn: what is it worth? It counts for nothing.

glosses.zh: 收骨肉：收殓亲人的尸骨。骨肉，亲人。
glosses.en: shōu gǔ ròu: to gather and bury the bodies of one's family. Gǔ ròu, bone and flesh, means close family.

glosses.zh: 世情：世上人的人情冷暖。
glosses.en: shì qíng: the way people of the world behave.

glosses.zh: 恶衰歇：讨厌已经衰败的人家。衰歇，衰落、败落。
glosses.en: wù shuāi xiē: to look down on a family that has fallen. Shuāi xiē means to decline.

glosses.zh: 随转烛：像风中摇晃的烛火一样，说变就变。
glosses.en: suí zhuǎn zhú: like a candle flame flickering in the wind, changing in a moment.

glosses.zh: 夫婿：丈夫。
glosses.en: fū xù: husband.

glosses.zh: 轻薄儿：轻浮、不讲情义的男人。
glosses.en: qīng bó ér: a fickle man with no loyalty.

glosses.zh: 新人：丈夫新娶的女子。
glosses.en: xīn rén: the new wife her husband has taken.

glosses.zh: 合昏：合欢树，又叫夜合花，叶子白天张开、晚上合拢，好像懂得时间。
glosses.en: hé hūn: the silk tree. Its leaves open by day and fold up at night, as if it knows the time.

glosses.zh: 鸳鸯：一种水鸟，总是雌雄成对生活，常用来比喻夫妻。
glosses.en: yuān yāng: mandarin ducks, which always live in pairs, a symbol of husband and wife.

glosses.zh: 不独宿：不会独自过夜。
glosses.en: bù dú sù: never sleep alone.

glosses.zh: 但见：只看见。但，只。
glosses.en: dàn jiàn: only sees. Dàn means only.

glosses.zh: 那闻：哪里听得见。
glosses.en: nǎ wén: how could he hear?

glosses.zh: 旧人：被抛弃的原来的妻子，就是这位佳人。
glosses.en: jiù rén: the old wife who has been cast off, that is, this lady.

glosses.zh: 在山泉水清：泉水在山里是清的。这一句和下一句是比喻，一般理解为：女子守住本心，就像山里的泉水一样清白。
glosses.en: zài shān quán shuǐ qīng: spring water in the hills is clear. This line and the next are a comparison, usually read as: a woman who keeps her true self stays pure like a mountain spring.

glosses.zh: 浊：浑浊，不干净。
glosses.en: zhuó: muddy, unclean.

glosses.zh: 侍婢：服侍她的丫鬟。
glosses.en: shì bì: her maid.

glosses.zh: 卖珠：卖掉珠宝首饰换钱过日子，说她已经很穷了。
glosses.en: mài zhū: selling pearls and jewels to live on, showing how poor she has become.

glosses.zh: 牵萝：拉来藤萝。萝，一种爬藤的植物。
glosses.en: qiān luó: pulling down vines. Luó is a climbing plant.

glosses.zh: 补茅屋：修补漏了的茅草屋。
glosses.en: bǔ máo wū: to mend the leaking thatched hut.

glosses.zh: 不插发：不往头上插，说她无心打扮。
glosses.en: bù chā fà: not putting them in her hair, for she has no heart to dress up.

glosses.zh: 柏：柏树，冬天也不落叶，常比喻坚贞的品格。
glosses.en: bǎi: the cypress, which stays green in winter, a symbol of a firm, faithful heart.

glosses.zh: 动盈掬：常常采满一把。动，往往；盈掬，满满一捧。
glosses.en: dòng yíng jū: often picks a full handful. Dòng means often; yíng jū means a full double handful.

glosses.zh: 翠袖：青绿色的衣袖。
glosses.en: cuì xiù: green sleeves.

glosses.zh: 倚：靠着。
glosses.en: yǐ: to lean against.

glosses.zh: 修竹：又高又长的竹子。修，长。
glosses.en: xiū zhú: tall, slender bamboo. Xiū means long.

translation.zh: 有一位世上少有的美人，
translation.en: There is a lady, fairest of her age,

translation.zh: 住在没有人烟的山谷里。
translation.en: living alone in an empty valley.

translation.zh: 她说自己是好人家的女儿，
translation.en: She says she comes from a good family,

translation.zh: 如今家道败落，只能靠着山林草木过活。
translation.en: but now she has fallen low and lives among the grass and trees.

translation.zh: 从前关中发生战乱，
translation.en: Long ago war tore through the land within the passes,

translation.zh: 她的兄弟都被杀害了。
translation.en: and her brothers were all killed.

translation.zh: 官做得再大又有什么用，
translation.en: What good were their high ranks?

translation.zh: 连他们的尸骨都没能收殓。
translation.en: No one could even gather their bones.

translation.zh: 世上的人情都讨厌已经败落的人家，
translation.en: The world turns its back on a family that has fallen;

translation.zh: 万事就像风中的烛火，说变就变。
translation.en: all things change like a candle flickering in the wind.

translation.zh: 她的丈夫是个轻薄的人，
translation.en: Her husband was a fickle man,

translation.zh: 又娶了一个美如玉的新人。
translation.en: and took a new wife as lovely as jade.

translation.zh: 合欢树尚且知道早开晚合，
translation.en: Even the silk tree knows when to fold its leaves at night,

translation.zh: 鸳鸯从来不会独自过夜。
translation.en: and mandarin ducks never sleep alone.

translation.zh: 丈夫只看见新人在笑，
translation.en: He sees only his new wife smile;

translation.zh: 哪里听得见旧人在哭？
translation.en: how could he hear his old wife cry?

translation.zh: 泉水在山里是清的，
translation.en: In the hills the spring runs clear;

translation.zh: 流出山就变浑了。
translation.en: out of the hills it turns muddy.

translation.zh: 丫鬟卖了珠宝回来，
translation.en: Her maid comes back from selling pearls,

translation.zh: 拉来藤萝修补茅屋。
translation.en: and pulls down vines to patch the thatched hut.

translation.zh: 她摘了花，却不插在头上，
translation.en: She picks flowers but does not put them in her hair;

translation.zh: 采来柏枝，常常是满满一把。
translation.en: she gathers cypress twigs, often a full handful.

translation.zh: 天气寒冷，她的翠绿衣袖很单薄，
translation.en: The day is cold and her green sleeves are thin;

translation.zh: 傍晚，她靠着高高的竹子站着。
translation.en: at dusk she leans against the tall bamboo.

background.zh: 这首诗写于唐肃宗乾元二年（759年）秋天。那时安史之乱还没有结束，关中又遇上大饥荒，杜甫辞去华州的小官，带着家人到秦州（今甘肃天水）逃荒。诗里写了一位在战乱中家破人亡、又被丈夫抛弃的女子。她是杜甫真的遇见过的人，还是杜甫借她来写自己的遭遇，历来说法不一。
background.en: This poem was written in the autumn of 759. The An Lushan Rebellion was still going on, and the land around Chang'an was hit by a great famine. Du Fu gave up a small post in Huazhou and took his family to Qinzhou, today's Tianshui in Gansu, to escape hunger. The poem tells of a woman whose family was destroyed in the war and whose husband then left her. Readers have long disagreed on whether she was someone Du Fu really met, or a figure he used to speak about his own fate.

author_note.zh: 杜甫（712—770），唐代大诗人，被人称为“诗圣”。他亲身经历了安史之乱，一家人四处逃难。他的诗常常写战乱中普通人的苦难，被称为“诗史”。他一心想为国家出力，却总是不被重用，这和诗中被抛弃却不改本心的佳人很相像。
author_note.en: Du Fu (712–770) was a great Tang poet, often called the Sage of Poetry. He lived through the An Lushan Rebellion and fled from place to place with his family. His poems often tell of ordinary people's suffering in war, so they are called a history in verse. He wanted with all his heart to serve his country but was never given real work, much like the lady in this poem who is cast aside yet keeps her true self.

appreciation.zh: 诗一开头，就把我们带进一座空空的山谷，那里住着一位绝美的女子。接着她自己讲身世：兄弟在战乱中被杀，家道败落，丈夫又娶了新人，只看见新人笑，听不见她哭。一个人的不幸，也照出了乱世里人情的冷暖。中间“在山泉水清，出山泉水浊”两句，像一句格言：守在山里的泉水才清澈。她虽然穷得要卖首饰、用藤萝补屋，却不打扮自己，只采常青的柏枝。最后一幅画最美：天冷了，她穿着单薄的翠袖，在黄昏里静静靠着修竹。竹子又直又有节，正像她不肯低头的品格。整首诗没有一句大声的抱怨，却让人心里久久放不下。
appreciation.en: The poem opens by leading us into an empty valley, where a very beautiful woman lives. Then she tells her own story. Her brothers were killed in the war, her family fell, and her husband took a new wife; he sees only the new wife smile and never hears her cry. One woman's bad luck also shows how cold people became in those hard times. In the middle, the lines about spring water clear in the hills and muddy outside are like a saying: water that stays in the hills stays pure. She is so poor that she sells her jewels and patches her hut with vines, yet she does not dress up; she picks only cypress, which stays green all winter. The last picture is the most beautiful. It is cold, her green sleeves are thin, and at dusk she leans quietly against the tall bamboo. Bamboo is straight and has firm joints, just like her character that will not bow. There is no loud complaint in the whole poem, yet it stays in the heart for a long time.
